summary: Kittitas County, WA lookout: a 1942 two-story smokehouse, then a 40-foot DNR tower (1962) removed or destroyed in 1970; the site now holds a fenced UW observatory.

facts.design: Two-story structure (1942), then a 40-foot wooden DNR tower (1962)
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1970 (sources differ on wording); the site now holds a fenced University of Washington observatory building

staffing.as_of: 1960 (lookout Barbara Gerwig, per DNR photo shoot)

access.note: Gated road (drivable to the top when the gate is open; seasonal closure from December 8 to May 1); observatory building fenced; WillhiteWeb says the site might be reached on foot as a long off-season hike from Ellensburg; UW says approved student groups can propose observing time

visit.trail_note: No lookout stands here; the site is a fenced observatory, so there is nothing to climb. WillhiteWeb says it might be reached on foot as a long off-season hike from Ellensburg.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says removed in 1970; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The year matches, so the record uses removed.

A 1998 Seattle Times (AP) report says UW was closing the Manastash Ridge Observatory; a UW observatory page describes it as open May through November. The sources read do not settle whether the closure happened, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Dates for the 1942 building, the 1962 tower and the 1970 end agree across sources; only the removed-versus-destroyed wording differs. The observatory's status is the open question: the 1998 AP report of a closure and the later UW page describing seasonal use do not reconcile in the sources read. Verification 2026-10-09: the earlier access level 'permission' and the claim that entry is by approval and the site is not open to casual visits were not supported by the WillhiteWeb page, which describes a gated road and a possible off-season hike; access was reclassified as restricted and the story corrected to match. The brief's record had no height; 40 feet (12.2 m) comes from the register and WillhiteWeb. The 1998 Seattle Times date is taken from the archive URL and the article's own text, which does not show a date line in the cached copy, so treat it as approximate to the year. The ADS abstract on the observatory's 1972 telescope and 2012 anniversary was seen only as a search snippet and is not cited.
